subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Fitness Literacy I: Training Principles Without Body Metrics

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of the health-related fitness components and what each one does in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe overload, progression, specificity, reversibility, and recovery using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply frequency, intensity, time, and type as design levers in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving monitoring effort by feel, breath, and speech; correct it and explain why.
Connect noticing capability change through what the learner can now do with evaluating fitness claims and products critically and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Design a four-week progression for one self-chosen capability and state how progress will be recognized through tasks the learner can perform — never through weight, size, body composition, or appearance.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated safe participation and self-management criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill cues or movement quality criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated tactical or training reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated self-assessment and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Fitness Literacy I: Training Principles Without Body Metrics?
